newsitem.title: HUNGARY: ABN-AMRO EXPANDS INSURANCE IN HUNGARY.
newsitem.headline: ABN-AMRO EXPANDS INSURANCE IN HUNGARY.

text.p: ABN-AMRO Bank's Hungarian life insurance unit on Friday announced the launch of a health service, adding Hungary as the seventh country in the world and the first in central Europe to provide access.
The service, available worldwide since January 1996, allows Hungarian patients to ask for the medical advice of U.S-based physicians as a second opinion after their local doctors.

"We wanted to provide a new service to our clients and this worldwide novelty was well timed," Andras Farkas, Deputy General Director of ABN-AMRO Magyar Elet- es Nyugdijbiztosito Rt, told a news conference on Friday.
Farkas told Reuters the product has been available in the Netherlands, UK, Israel, Italy, Greece and France.
The owner of the tele-diagnosis franchise is Netherland's Second Opinion International BV.

He added that ABM-AMRO's Hungarian life and pension unit had some 1,000 clients since the launch of the unit in May, and hopes to boost their numbers to between 30,000 and 40,000 by the end of the year.
Farkas added that a survey they had made on more than 70,000 people showed that 90 percent showed interest in the new product.

The Dutch banking group ABN-AMRO has been expanding in Hungary and in central and eastern Europe as well. Last year it had bought an 89.23 percent stake in Magyar Hitel Bank and made a buyout offer for the rest of the shares.
On Thursday, ABN-AMRO chairman Jan Kalff said in Budapest the bank was considering buying more banks in eastern and central Europe.
